title.zh: 卷一百八十七 列傳第七十四: 烏古孫良楨 賈魯 逯魯曾 貢師泰 周伯琦 吳當
title.en: Volume 187 Biographies 74: Wugusunliangzhen, Jia Lu, Lu Luceng, Gong Shitai, Zhou Boqi, Wu Dang
title.raw: 卷一百八十七 列傳第七十四: 烏古孫良楨 賈魯 逯魯曾 貢師泰 周伯琦 吳當 Volume 187 Biographies 74: Wugusunliangzhen, Jia Lu, Lu Luceng, Gong Shitai, Zhou Boqi, Wu Dang

sentences.zh: 烏古孫良楨

translations.literal: Wugusun Liangzhen
translations.idiomatic: Wugusun Liangzhen

sentences.zh: 烏古孫良楨字幹卿，世次見父澤傳。

translations.literal: Wugusun Liangzhen, style name Ganqing; his place in the lineage is given in his father Ze's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Wugusun Liangzhen, whose courtesy name was Ganqing, is treated further in the genealogical account in his father Ze's biography.

sentences.zh: 資器絕人，好讀書。

translations.literal: His native endowment and capacity surpassed others; he loved to read books.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted beyond ordinary men, he devoted himself to learning.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，蔭補江陰州判官，尋丁內艱，服除，調婺州武義縣尹，有惠政。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi, he entered office by inherited privilege as assistant prefect of Jiangyin prefecture; soon he mourned his mother, and when the mourning ended he was transferred to magistrate of Wuyi county in Wuzhou, where he had benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: In 1322 he inherited his father's privilege and was appointed assistant prefect of Jiangyin; shortly afterward he went into mourning for his mother. After the mourning period he was assigned magistrate of Wuyi in Wuzhou, where he earned a reputation for humane governance.

sentences.zh: 改漳州路推官，獄有疑者，悉平反之。

translations.literal: He was changed to judicial investigator of Zhangzhou circuit; in cases where imprisonment was doubtful, he reversed all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to serve as judicial investigator on the Zhangzhou circuit, he overturned every conviction he found questionable.

sentences.zh: 上言：「律，徒者不杖，今杖而又徒，非恤刑意，宜加徒減杖。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "By the statutes, those sentenced to penal servitude are not to be caned; now they are caned and also sentenced to penal servitude—this does not accord with the intent of merciful punishment; penal servitude should be increased and caning reduced."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne: "The law provides that those sentenced to penal servitude shall not also be flogged; yet offenders are now flogged and then sentenced to penal servitude as well. That is not the spirit of lenient punishment. The statute should be amended to increase the term of penal servitude and reduce the number of strokes."

sentences.zh: 」遂定為令。

translations.literal: "This was then fixed as a statute.
translations.idiomatic: The reform was duly enacted as law.

sentences.zh: 移泉州，益以能稱。

translations.literal: He was moved to Quanzhou, and his reputation for competence grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to Quanzhou, he won still greater renown for his ability.

sentences.zh: 轉延平判官，拜陝西行臺監察御史，劾遼陽行省左丞相達識帖睦邇賣國不忠，援漢高帝斬丁公故事，以明人臣大義。

translations.literal: He was transferred to judicial investigator of Yanping, appointed investigating censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, and impeached Dashi Timur, Left Chancellor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, for selling out the state and disloyalty, citing the precedent of Han Emperor Gaozu executing Lord Ding to clarify the great righteousness owed by subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to judicial investigator at Yanping and then appointed investigating censor on the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, he impeached Dashi Timur, left chancellor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, for betraying the state. Invoking the Han precedent of Emperor Gaozu executing Lord Ding, he argued to make plain the supreme duty owed by a subject to his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 并劾御史中丞胡居祐奸邪，皆罷之，中外震懾。

translations.literal: He also impeached Vice Censor-in-Chief Hu Juyou for wickedness and depravity; both were dismissed, and court and country were shaken with awe.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Vice Censor-in-Chief Hu Juyou for corruption and treachery. Both men were removed from office, and the whole empire was shaken.

sentences.zh: 陞都事，猶以言不盡行，解去。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of affairs, but because his words were not fully carried out, he resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to director of affairs, he resigned when his recommendations were not fully implemented.

sentences.zh: 復起為監察御史，良楨以帝方覽萬幾，不可不求賢自輔，於是連疏：「天曆數年間紀綱大壞，元氣傷夷。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed investigating censor; Liangzhen, considering that the emperor was just then reviewing the myriad affairs of state and could not but seek worthy men to assist him, thereupon submitted successive memorials: "During the Tianshun years the statutes and ordinances were greatly corrupted and the vital energies of the state were injured and weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve again as investigating censor, Liangzhen judged that with the emperor now personally attending to the myriad affairs of government, he could not afford to neglect recruiting worthy advisers. He therefore submitted a series of memorials: "During the Tianshun era the laws and institutions fell into grave disorder and the vital energies of the dynasty were grievously depleted.

sentences.zh: 天祐聖明，入膺大統，而西宮秉政，奸臣弄權，畜憾十有餘年。

translations.literal: Heaven blessed his sagely brilliance, and he received the great succession; yet the Western Palace held power, wicked ministers manipulated authority, and resentment was nursed for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven blessed Your Sagely Brilliance to ascend the great succession, yet the Western Palace held the reins of power, wicked ministers manipulated authority, and grievances festered for more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 天威一怒，陰晦開明，以正大名，以章大孝，此誠兢兢業業祈天永命之秋，其術在乎敬身修德而已。

translations.literal: When Heaven's majesty was roused to anger, obscurity gave way to brightness; the great name was rectified and great filial piety was displayed—this is truly the season for trembling diligence in praying Heaven for enduring mandate; the method lies only in revering the person and cultivating virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven's wrath was unleashed, darkness gave way to light; the imperial name was set right and filial piety was proclaimed to the world. This is truly the moment to serve Heaven with trembling diligence and pray for an enduring mandate—and the means lie solely in self-restraint and the cultivation of virtue.

sentences.zh: 今經筵多領以職事臣，數日一進講，不渝數刻已罷，而御小臣，恒侍左右，何益於盛德哉。

translations.literal: Now at the Classics Lecture many who lead it are officials with other duties; they lecture once every several days and do not exceed a few moments before finishing, while minor attendants constantly wait at the left and right—what benefit is this to magnificent virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Today the Classics Lecture is led mostly by officials burdened with other duties. They lecture only once every few days and dismiss the session after a few moments, while petty attendants linger constantly at Your side. What good can this do for the cultivation of imperial virtue?

sentences.zh: 臣願招延儒臣若許衡者數人，置於禁密，常以唐、虞、三代之道，啟沃宸衷，日新其德，實萬世無疆之福也。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to summon and retain several Confucian ministers such as Xu Heng, place them within the inner precincts, and constantly use the ways of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties to enrich the imperial heart, renewing virtue day by day—this would truly be blessing without boundary for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that several Confucian scholars of Xu Heng's stature be summoned to serve within the inner palace, there to instruct Your Majesty continually in the ways of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, renewing Your virtue day by day. That would be a blessing without limit for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 」又以國俗父死則妻其從母，兄弟死則收其妻，父母死無憂制，遂言：「綱常皆出於天而不可變，議法之吏，乃言國人不拘此例，諸國人各從本俗。

translations.literal: "He also said that by national custom, when the father dies one marries his father's younger brother's wife; when a brother dies one takes his brother's wife; when parents die there is no mourning observance—thereupon he said: "The constants of human relations all come from Heaven and cannot be changed; yet the officials who deliberate on law say that Mongols are not bound by this rule and that people of the various states each follow their native customs.
translations.idiomatic: He also addressed Mongol customs by which a man marries his stepmother after his father's death, takes his brother's widow after a brother's death, and observes no mourning when parents die. He wrote: "The moral order proceeds from Heaven and cannot be altered. Yet the officials who draft legislation hold that Mongols need not observe these rules and that peoples of every realm may follow their native customs.

sentences.zh: 是漢、南人當守綱常，國人、諸國人不必守綱常也。

translations.literal: This means that Han Chinese and southerners must observe the constants of human relations, while Mongols and peoples of the various states need not observe them.
translations.idiomatic: In effect this means that Han Chinese and southerners must uphold the moral order, while Mongols and other subject peoples need not.

sentences.zh: 名曰優之，實則陷之，外若尊之，內實侮之，推其本心所以待國人者，不若漢、南人之厚也。

translations.literal: It is called treating them with favor, but in reality it traps them; outwardly they seem to be honored, but inwardly they are truly insulted—pushing to the bottom of the heart how Mongols are treated, it is not as generous as toward Han Chinese and southerners.
translations.idiomatic: What is called favor in name is entrapment in fact; what appears respect outwardly is contempt within. At bottom Mongols are treated less generously than Han Chinese and southerners.

sentences.zh: 請下禮官有司及右科進士在朝者會議，自天子至於庶人，皆從禮制，以成列聖未遑之典，明萬世不易之道。

translations.literal: He requested that ritual officials, responsible agencies, and jinshi of the Right Branch in court confer, and that from the Son of Heaven down to the common people all follow ritual regulations, thereby completing the canon that successive sages had not yet had leisure to establish and clarifying the Way unchanging for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that ritual officials, the responsible agencies, and jinshi of the Right Branch now at court be ordered to deliberate together, and that from the Son of Heaven to the common people all alike follow the ritual code—thereby completing the canon our sage forebears had not yet had leisure to enact and making plain the Way that must not change for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「隱士劉因，道學經術可比許文正公衡，從祀孔子廟庭。

translations.literal: "He also said: "The recluse Liu Yin, in the learning of the Way and classical studies, may be compared to Duke of Culture Xu Heng; he should be granted accompanying sacrifice in the court of Confucius's temple.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that the recluse Liu Yin, whose mastery of the Way and classical learning rivaled that of Duke of Culture Xu Heng, be granted accompanying sacrifice in the temple of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 」皆不報。

translations.literal: "None received reply.
translations.idiomatic: None of these proposals received a response.

sentences.zh: 御史臺作新風憲，復疏其所當行者，以舉賢才為綱，而以厚風俗、均賦役、重審理、汰冗官、選守令、出奉使、均公田為目，指擿剴切，雖觸忌諱，亦不顧也。

translations.literal: When the Censorate drew up new regulations for the wind of the law, he again memorialized what ought to be carried out: taking the promotion of worthy talent as the guiding principle, with enriching customs, equalizing tax and corvée labor, emphasizing judicial review, eliminating redundant officials, selecting prefects and magistrates, dispatching imperial envoys, and equalizing public fields as the headings—his finger-pointing was incisive and cutting, and even when he touched taboos he did not care.
translations.idiomatic: When the Censorate promulgated new regulations for censorial oversight, he submitted another memorial setting forth what ought to be done: promoting worthy talent as the overarching principle, with enriching customs, equalizing taxes and corvée, strengthening judicial review, eliminating redundant officials, selecting prefects and magistrates, dispatching imperial envoys, and equalizing public fields as specific aims. His criticisms were sharp and unsparing; even when they touched forbidden topics he did not hold back.

sentences.zh: 宦者罕失嬖妾殺其妻，糜其肉飼犬，上疏乞正重刑，并論宦寺結廷臣撓政為害，可汰黜之。

translations.literal: A eunuch named Han, having lost a favored concubine, killed his wife, ground her flesh, and fed it to dogs; he submitted a memorial requesting severe punishment be applied, and also discussed how eunuchs banding with court ministers to obstruct government was harmful and they could be eliminated and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When a eunuch named Han, having lost a favored concubine, killed his wife, minced her flesh, and fed it to his dogs, Liangzhen memorialized asking that the severest penalty be imposed. He also argued that eunuchs who colluded with court officials to obstruct government were a grave evil and ought to be purged.

sentences.zh: 憸佞側目。

translations.literal: The sycophantic and the servile glared sideways at him.
translations.idiomatic: The sycophants and flatterers glared at him with hatred.

sentences.zh: 至正四年，召為刑部員外郎，轉御史臺都事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhizheng, he was summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Punishments, then transferred to director of affairs of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1344 he was summoned to serve as vice director in the Ministry of Punishments and was soon transferred to director of affairs at the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 五年，改中書左司都事，出為江東道肅政廉訪司副使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was changed to director of affairs of the Left Department of the Secretariat, then sent out as vice commissioner of the Jiangdong Surveillance Commission for Purification of Government.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed director of affairs in the Secretariat's Left Department, then posted as vice commissioner of the Jiangdong Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 上官一日，辭歸。

translations.literal: He took office for one day, then resigned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He assumed the post for a single day and then resigned.

sentences.zh: 六年，授平江路緫管，不拜。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was appointed general administrator of Pingjiang circuit but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In 1346 he was offered the post of general administrator of Pingjiang circuit but declined to accept it.

sentences.zh: 八年，復召為右司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was again summoned as vice director of the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: In 1348 he was recalled to serve as vice director of the Secretariat's Right Department.

sentences.zh: 九年，陞郎中，尋遷廣東道肅政廉訪使，未行，還為郎中，遷福建道肅政廉訪使，中道召還，參議中書省事，兼經筵官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to director; soon he was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Guangdong circuit, but before departing he returned to serve as director, was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Fujian circuit, was summoned back en route, and became participant in Secretariat affairs, concurrently serving as Classics Lecture official.
translations.idiomatic: In 1349 he was promoted to director, then appointed surveillance commissioner of the Guangdong circuit but recalled before he could take up the post. Reappointed director, he was next assigned surveillance commissioner of Fujian, then summoned back while still en route and made a participant in Secretariat affairs, concurrently serving at the Classics Lecture.

sentences.zh: 十一年，拜治書侍御史，陞中書參知政事、同知經筵事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was appointed supervising censor, promoted to participant in government of the Secretariat and associate director of Classics Lecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1351 he was appointed supervising censor, then promoted to vice grand councillor of the Secretariat and associate director of the Classics Lecture.

sentences.zh: 十三年，陞左丞，兼大司農卿，仍同知經筵事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was promoted to left vice grand councillor, concurrently Minister of the Great Agrarian Office, and still associate director of Classics Lecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1353 he was promoted to left vice grand councillor and concurrent minister of the Great Agrarian Office, retaining his post as associate director of the Classics Lecture.

sentences.zh: 時中書參用非人，事多異同，不得一一如志。

translations.literal: At that time the Secretariat employed unworthy men, affairs often differed in opinion, and he could not carry out his will in every respect.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was then staffed with unworthy men; policies were constantly disputed, and he could not always carry out his intentions.

sentences.zh: 會軍餉不給，請與右丞悟良哈台主屯田，歲入二十萬石。

translations.literal: When military provisions were insufficient, he requested together with Right Vice Councillor Ulabqatai to oversee garrison farming, with annual intake of two hundred thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: When military provisions ran short, he joined Right Vice Councillor Ulabqatai in supervising garrison agriculture, producing two hundred thousand piculs of grain annually.

sentences.zh: 東宮久未建，懇懇為言，車駕幸上都，始冊皇太子。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace had long gone unestablished; he pleaded earnestly on the matter, and when the imperial carriage visited the Upper Capital, the crown prince was at last installed.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent had long gone uninstalled; Liangzhen pleaded earnestly on the matter, and when the emperor traveled to the Upper Capital the crown prince was at last formally designated.

sentences.zh: 立詹事院，驛召為副詹事，每直端本堂，則進正心誠意之說、親君子遠小人之道，皇太子嘉納焉。

translations.literal: When the Household of the Heir Apparent was established, he was summoned by post as vice household head; whenever he attended at the Hall of the Upright Root, he advanced teachings on rectifying the mind and making intentions sincere, and on drawing near to gentlemen and keeping distant from petty men—the crown prince praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Household of the Heir Apparent was established, he was summoned by urgent dispatch to serve as vice household head. Whenever he attended at the Hall of the Upright Root he instructed the crown prince in rectifying the mind and making the intentions sincere, and in drawing near to gentlemen while keeping petty men at a distance. The crown prince received his teaching with approval.

sentences.zh: 當時盜賊蜂起，帝聞，惡之，下詔分討，必盡誅而後已。

translations.literal: At that time bandits and robbers swarmed forth; when the emperor heard of it he detested them and issued an edict for separate pursuit, insisting they must all be executed before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits and rebels were then rising everywhere. When the emperor heard of it he was enraged and issued an edict ordering separate campaigns of suppression, decreeing that none were to be spared until all had been exterminated.

sentences.zh: 良楨言：「平賊在收人心，以回天意，多殺非道也。

translations.literal: Liangzhen said: "Pacifying bandits lies in winning people's hearts and turning back Heaven's intent; mass killing is not the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhen said: "To pacify rebellion one must win back the people's hearts and turn Heaven's wrath. Mass slaughter is not the Way."

sentences.zh: 」乃赦以安之。

translations.literal: "Thereupon an amnesty was issued to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty was accordingly proclaimed to reassure the populace.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷淮南行省左丞。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was transferred to left vice grand councillor of the Huainan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1354 he was transferred to left vice grand councillor of the Huainan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，泰州賊張士誠既降復叛，殺淮南行省參知政事趙璉，進據高郵、六合，太師脫脫奉詔，緫諸王軍南征，而良楨洎參議龔伯璲、刑部主事廬山等從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Taizhou bandit Zhang Shicheng had submitted and then rebelled again, killing Participant in Government Zhao Lian of the Huainan Branch Secretariat and advancing to occupy Gaoyou and Luhe; Grand Preceptor Toghto received the edict and commanded the armies of the imperial princes on a southern campaign, and Liangzhen together with Participant Gong Bojuan, director of affairs Lu Shan of the Ministry of Punishments, and others followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Taizhou rebel Zhang Shicheng had surrendered and then rebelled again, killing Zhao Lian, participant in government of the Huainan Branch Secretariat, and seizing Gaoyou and Luhe. Grand Preceptor Toghto received orders to command the armies of the imperial princes on a southern campaign, and Liangzhen went with him, accompanied by Participant Gong Bojuan, Lu Shan of the Ministry of Punishments, and others.

sentences.zh: 既平六合，垂克高郵，會詔罷脫脫兵柄，遂有上變告伯璲等勸脫脫勒兵北向者，下其事逮問，詞連良楨，簿對無所驗。

translations.literal: After Luhe was pacified and Gaoyou was on the verge of capture, an edict arrived removing Toghto from military command; thereupon someone submitted a report of irregularity accusing Gong Bojuan and others of urging Toghto to force the army northward; the matter was sent down for arrest and interrogation, implicating Liangzhen in the testimony, but examination of the records found nothing verified.
translations.idiomatic: After Luhe was pacified and Gaoyou was nearly taken, an edict arrived stripping Toghto of military command. Someone then submitted a report accusing Gong Bojuan and others of urging Toghto to march the army north against the court. The case was sent down for arrest and interrogation, and Liangzhen was implicated in the testimony, but examination of the records found no evidence against him.

sentences.zh: 即日還中書左丞，命分省彰德，主調軍食，居半歲，還中書。

translations.literal: That same day he returned as left vice grand councillor of the Secretariat, was ordered to branch-secretariat at Zhangde to oversee provisioning of military grain, and after half a year returned to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was restored as left vice grand councillor of the Secretariat, then ordered to the Zhangde branch secretariat to oversee military provisions. After half a year he returned to the central government.

sentences.zh: 十六年，進階榮祿大夫，賜玉帶一。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was advanced in rank to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and granted one jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: In 1356 he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and granted a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 十七年，除大司農。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was appointed Minister of the Great Agrarian Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1357 he was appointed minister of the Great Agrarian Office.

sentences.zh: 明年，陞右丞，兼大司農，辭，不允。

translations.literal: The next year, he was promoted to right vice grand councillor, concurrently Great Agrarian minister; he declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to right vice grand councillor while retaining the Great Agrarian portfolio. He declined but was not permitted to resign.

sentences.zh: 論罷陷賊延坐之令。

translations.literal: He argued for abolishing the statute of collective punishment for those implicated with bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He argued successfully for abolishing the statute imposing collective punishment on families of those accused of colluding with rebels.

sentences.zh: 有惡少年誣知宜興州張復通賊之罪，中書將籍其孥，吏抱案請署。

translations.literal: A vicious youth falsely accused Zhang Fu, prefect of Yixing, of communicating with bandits; the Secretariat was about to register his household for confiscation, and a clerk brought the dossier requesting signature.
translations.idiomatic: A vicious youth falsely accused Zhang Fu, prefect of Yixing, of communicating with rebels. The Secretariat was about to register his family for confiscation, and a clerk brought the dossier for Liangzhen's signature.

sentences.zh: 良楨曰；

translations.literal: Liangzhen said:
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhen said:

sentences.zh: 「手可斷，案不可署。

translations.literal: "My hand may be cut off, but this dossier I will not sign.
translations.idiomatic: "My hand may be severed, but I will not sign this dossier."

sentences.zh: 」同列變色，卒不署。

translations.literal: "His colleagues changed color, but in the end he did not sign.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues turned pale, but in the end he refused to sign.

sentences.zh: 良楨自左曹登政府，多所建白。

translations.literal: Liangzhen, from the Left Department ascending to government, made many proposals.
translations.idiomatic: From his rise through the Left Department to the highest councils of state, Liangzhen offered many constructive proposals.

sentences.zh: 罷福建、山東食鹽，浙東、西長生牛租，瀕海被災圍田稅，民皆德之。

translations.literal: He abolished the salt monopoly in Fujian and Shandong, the long-life ox rent in eastern and western Zhe, and the enclosed-field tax on coastal disaster victims—the people all regarded him with virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the salt monopoly in Fujian and Shandong, the long-life ox levy in eastern and western Zhe, and the enclosed-field tax on coastal lands stricken by disaster. The people everywhere blessed his name.

sentences.zh: 嘗論至正格輕重不倫，吏得並緣為奸，舉明律者數人，參酌古今，重定律書，書成而罷。

translations.literal: He once argued that the Zhizheng code's gradations of severity were inconsistent, allowing clerks to exploit both and commit fraud; he nominated several who understood the Ming code, consulted past and present, and redrafted the law book—the book was completed but the project was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: He once argued that the Zhizheng code's gradations of punishment were inconsistent, allowing clerks to exploit the gaps for fraud. He nominated several experts in the Ming code to consult past and present precedents and redraft the statutes. The new code was completed, but the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 家居輒訓諸子曰：「吾無過人者，惟待人以誠，人亦以誠遇我，汝宜志之。

translations.literal: At home he would instruct his sons, saying: "I have nothing surpassing others except treating people with sincerity; people also treat me with sincerity—you should keep this in mind.
translations.idiomatic: At home he would instruct his sons: "I have no special gift beyond this: I treat others with sincerity, and they respond in kind. Remember that."

sentences.zh: 」晚歲病瘠，數謁告，病益侵，遂卒。

translations.literal: "In his later years he grew thin from illness, repeatedly requested leave, his illness grew worse, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he grew gaunt from illness, repeatedly requested leave, and as his condition worsened he died.

sentences.zh: 自號約齋。

translations.literal: He styled himself Master of the Compact Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He took the style Master of the Compact Studio.

sentences.zh: 有詩文奏議凡若干卷，藏于家。

translations.literal: He had poetry, prose, and memorials totaling several juan, kept in his household.
translations.idiomatic: His collected poetry, prose, and memorials, comprising several juan, were preserved by his family.

sentences.zh: 賈魯字友恒，河東高平人。

translations.literal: Jia Lu, style name Youheng, was a native of Gaoping in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Lu, whose courtesy name was Youheng, came from Gaoping in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 幼負志節，既長，謀略過人。

translations.literal: In youth he bore lofty resolve; when grown, his stratagems surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he showed firmness of purpose; when grown, his strategic judgment surpassed that of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 延祐、至治間，兩以明經領鄉貢。

translations.literal: Between the Yanyou and Zhizhi reigns, twice he led the provincial recommendation through mastery of the Classics.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanyou and Zhizhi reigns he twice led his district's candidates in the provincial examinations through mastery of the Classics.

sentences.zh: 泰定初，恩授東平路儒學教授，辟憲史，歷行省掾，除潞城縣尹，選丞相東曹掾，擢戶部主事，未上。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiding, by grace he was appointed professor of the Confucian school of Dongping circuit, was recruited as secretarial aide to the surveillance commissioner, served as secretariat aide of the branch secretariat, was appointed magistrate of Lucheng county, was selected as secretarial aide of the Chancellor's Eastern Department, was promoted to director of affairs in the Ministry of Revenue, but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taiding reign he was granted by imperial favor the post of professor at the Confucian school of Dongping circuit. He was recruited as a surveillance secretarial aide, served as a branch secretariat aide, was appointed magistrate of Lucheng, selected as secretarial aide in the Chancellor's Eastern Department, and promoted to director of affairs in the Ministry of Revenue—but never took up the last appointment.

sentences.zh: 一日，覺心悸，尋得父書，筆勢顫縮，即辭歸，比至家，父已有風疾，未幾卒。

translations.literal: One day he felt palpitations of the heart; soon he received a letter from his father whose brushwork trembled and shrank; he immediately resigned and returned, and by the time he reached home his father already had wind affliction and before long died.
translations.idiomatic: One day he felt his heart palpitate. Soon a letter arrived from his father, the brushstrokes trembling and contracted. He resigned at once and hurried home, but by the time he arrived his father was already stricken with paralysis and died shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 魯居喪服闋，起為太醫院都事。

translations.literal: Lu, when mourning ended, was recalled as director of affairs of the Imperial Medical Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period Jia Lu was recalled to serve as director of affairs at the Imperial Medical Academy.

sentences.zh: 會詔修遼、金、宋三史，召魯為宋史局官。

translations.literal: When an edict was issued to compile the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song, Lu was summoned as an official of the Song History Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered the compilation of the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song, he was summoned to serve in the Song History Bureau.

sentences.zh: 書成，選魯燕南山東道奉使宣撫幕官，考績居最，遷中書省檢校官。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, Lu was selected as staff officer on the pacification commission of the Yanshan-Shandong circuit, ranked highest in performance evaluation, and was transferred to revising official of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the histories were completed he was selected as staff officer on the Yanshan-Shandong pacification commission, ranked first in performance evaluation, and transferred to revising official of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上言：「十八河倉，近歲淪沒官糧百三十萬斛，其弊由富民兼并，貧民流亡，宜合先正經界，然事體重大，非處置盡善，不可輕發。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "At the Eighteen Rivers granaries, in recent years one million three hundred thousand hu of official grain have been lost to inundation; the abuse stems from wealthy households engrossing land while poor people flee and become displaced—it is fitting first to rectify the field boundaries, yet the matter is weighty and unless disposed of with complete soundness it must not be lightly launched.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "At the Eighteen Rivers granaries, more than 1.3 million hu of state grain have been lost to inundation in recent years. The root of the abuse lies in wealthy households engrossing land while the poor flee as refugees. Field boundaries should first be rectified—but the matter is grave, and unless every measure is soundly planned it must not be undertaken lightly."

sentences.zh: 」書累數萬言，切中其弊。

translations.literal: "His document accumulated to tens of thousands of words and struck to the heart of the abuses.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial ran to tens of thousands of words and struck to the heart of the abuses.

sentences.zh: 俄拜監察御史，首言御史有封事，宜專達聖聰，不宜臺臣先有所可否。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed investigating censor and first said that when censors have sealed memorials, they should reach the sacred ear alone and censorate members should not first express approval or disapproval.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed investigating censor. His first memorial held that sealed memorials from censors should reach the emperor directly, without censorate colleagues prejudging them by expressing approval or disapproval in advance.

sentences.zh: 陞臺都事，遷山北廉訪副使，復召為工部郎中，言考工一十九事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of affairs of the Censorate, transferred to vice surveillance commissioner of the Shanbei circuit, was again summoned as director in the Ministry of Works, and spoke on nineteen matters of works inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to director of affairs at the Censorate, then transferred to vice surveillance commissioner of the Shanbei circuit, he was recalled to serve as director in the Ministry of Works and submitted nineteen recommendations on works administration.

sentences.zh: 至正四年，河決白茅堤，又決金堤，並河郡邑，民居昏墊，壯者流離。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhizheng, the Yellow River burst the Baimao dike and also burst the Jindi; counties and prefectures along the river had dwellings drowned in darkness, and strong men became displaced wanderers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1344 the Yellow River burst the Baimao dike and then the Jindi embankment as well. Towns and villages along the river were submerged; able-bodied men fled as refugees.

sentences.zh: 帝甚患之，遣使體驗，仍督大臣訪求治河方略，特命魯行都水監。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply troubled, sent envoys to investigate on the spot, and still urged the great ministers to seek strategies for controlling the river; he specially ordered Lu to act as director of the Directorate of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply troubled. He dispatched envoys to inspect the damage on the spot and ordered his ministers to seek strategies for controlling the river. Jia Lu was specially appointed acting director of the Directorate of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 魯循行河道，考察地形，往復數千里，備得要害，為圖上進二策：其一，議修築北堤，以制橫潰，則用工省；

translations.literal: Lu traveled the river course, examined the terrain, went back and forth several thousand li, gathered all critical points, and submitted a diagram with two strategies: the first, proposing to build and repair the northern dike to control lateral breaches, would use labor sparingly;
translations.idiomatic: Jia Lu traveled the river course, surveyed the terrain, and journeyed back and forth over several thousand li until he had mastered every critical point. He submitted a map with two proposed strategies: the first, to build and repair the northern dike to contain lateral breaches, would require relatively little labor;

sentences.zh: 其一，議疏塞並舉，挽河東行，使復故道，其功數倍。

translations.literal: the second, proposing dredging and blocking together, drawing the river eastward to restore the old course, would require several times the labor.
translations.idiomatic: the second, to dredge and block simultaneously and draw the river eastward back to its old course, would require several times the effort.

sentences.zh: 會遷右司郎中，議未及竟。

translations.literal: Just then he was transferred to director of the Right Department, and the deliberation did not reach completion.
translations.idiomatic: Just then he was transferred to director of the Right Department, and deliberation on the plans was cut short.

sentences.zh: 其在右司，言時政二十一事，皆見舉行。

translations.literal: While in the Right Department, he spoke on twenty-one matters of current policy, all of which were adopted and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Right Department he submitted twenty-one recommendations on current policy, all of which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 調都漕運使，復以漕事二十事言之，朝廷取其八事：一曰京畿和糴，二曰優恤漕司舊領漕戶，三曰接連委官，四曰通州緫治豫定委官，五曰船戶困於壩夫，海運壞於壩戶，六曰疏濬運河，七曰臨清運糧萬戶府當隸漕司，八曰宣忠船戶付本司節制。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Metropolitan Grain Transport, and again spoke on twenty matters of transport; the court adopted eight of them: first, government purchase of grain in the capital region; second, preferential relief for transport households formerly under the transport office; third, continuous appointment of officials; fourth, overall governance at Tongzhou with pre-designated appointees; fifth, boat households oppressed by dam laborers and sea transport ruined by dam households; sixth, dredging the Grand Canal; seventh, the Linqing grain-transport ten-thousand-household office should be subordinate to the transport office; eighth, the Xuanzhong boat households should be placed under this office's control.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to commissioner of metropolitan grain transport, he submitted twenty recommendations on transport affairs. The court adopted eight: government purchase of grain in the capital region; preferential relief for transport households formerly under the transport office; continuous appointment of supervisory officials; overall governance at Tongzhou with officials designated in advance; relief for boat households oppressed by dam laborers and for sea transport disrupted by dam households; dredging of the Grand Canal; subordination of the Linqing grain-transport ten-thousand-household office to the transport commission; and placing the Xuanzhong boat households under the commission's direct control.

sentences.zh: 事未盡行。

translations.literal: The matters were not fully carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining recommendations were not fully implemented.

sentences.zh: 既而河水北侵安山，淪入運河，延袤濟南、河間，將隳兩漕司鹽場，實妨國計。

translations.literal: Before long the river water invaded Anshan from the north, sank into the Grand Canal, and extended across Jinan and Hejian, about to destroy the salt fields of both transport offices—this truly obstructed the national revenue plan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the river invaded Anshan from the north and poured into the Grand Canal, spreading across Jinan and Hejian and threatening to destroy the salt fields of both transport commissions—a grave blow to state revenue.

sentences.zh: 九年，太傅、右丞相脫脫復相，論及河決，思拯民艱，以塞詔旨，乃集廷臣群議，言人人殊。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Grand Tutor and Right Chancellor Toghto returned to office; when the river breach was discussed, thinking to relieve the people's hardship and satisfy the imperial edict, he gathered court ministers for collective deliberation, and each man's words differed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1352 Grand Tutor and Right Chancellor Toghto returned to power. When the river breach was discussed, wishing to relieve the people's suffering and fulfill the imperial mandate, he convened the court for collective deliberation—but every minister had a different opinion.

sentences.zh: 魯昌言：「河必當治。

translations.literal: Lu spoke forthrightly: "The river must be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Lu spoke forthrightly: "The river must be brought under control."

sentences.zh: 」復以前二策進，丞相取其後策，與魯定議，且以其事屬魯。

translations.literal: "He again advanced the previous two strategies; the chancellor took the latter strategy, settled the plan with Lu, and entrusted the matter to him.
translations.idiomatic: He again presented his two earlier strategies. The chancellor chose the second, settled the plan with Jia Lu, and entrusted the entire project to him.

sentences.zh: 魯固辭，丞相曰：「此事非子不可。

translations.literal: Lu firmly declined; the chancellor said: "This matter cannot be done without you.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Lu firmly declined, but the chancellor said, "This cannot be accomplished without you."

sentences.zh: 」乃入奏，大稱帝旨。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he entered to memorialize, and it greatly accorded with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized the throne, and the proposal met with the emperor's full approval.

sentences.zh: 十一年四月，命魯以工部尚書、緫治河防使，進秩二品，授以銀章，領河南、北諸路軍民，發汴梁、大名十有三路民一十五萬，廬州等戍十有八翼軍二萬供役，一切從事大小軍民官，咸稟節度，便宜興繕。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eleventh year, Lu was ordered as Minister of Works and overall commissioner for river defense, advanced to second rank, granted a silver seal, to command military and civilian personnel of all circuits in Henan and the north; from thirteen circuits including Bianliang and Daming, one hundred fifty thousand civilians were mobilized, and from eighteen garrison wings including Luzhou, twenty thousand troops were supplied for labor; all officials great and small, military and civilian, were under his command, with discretionary authority to undertake construction.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 1351 Jia Lu was appointed minister of works and overall commissioner for river defense, advanced to second rank, and granted a silver seal. He was given command over military and civilian personnel throughout Henan and the north. From thirteen circuits including Bianliang and Daming he mobilized 150,000 civilians; from eighteen garrison wings including Luzhou he supplied 20,000 troops for labor. All officials, military and civilian, great and small, were placed under his command with discretionary authority to undertake whatever construction was required.

sentences.zh: 是月鳩工，七月鑿河成，八月決水故河，九月舟楫通，十一月諸埽諸堤成，水土工畢，河復故道。

translations.literal: That month labor was assembled; in the seventh month the river channel was cut and completed; in the eighth month water was released into the old course; in the ninth month boats and oars passed; in the eleventh month all revetments and dikes were completed, earth and water works finished, and the river restored its old course.
translations.idiomatic: That month work crews were assembled. In the seventh month the new channel was completed. In the eighth month the sluice was opened into the old course. By the ninth month boats were passing freely. In the eleventh month all revetments and dikes were finished, earthworks and waterworks completed, and the river restored to its ancient channel.

sentences.zh: 事見河渠志。

translations.literal: The affair is recorded in the Treatise on Rivers and Canals.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the Treatise on Rivers and Canals.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使報祭河伯，召魯還京師，魯以河平圖獻。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to report the sacrifice to the River Lord and summoned Lu back to the capital; Lu presented a diagram of the pacified river.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched envoys to report the sacrifice to the River Lord and summoned Jia Lu back to the capital, where he presented a map of the pacified river.

sentences.zh: 帝適覽臺臣奏疏，請褒脫脫治河之績，次論魯功，超拜榮祿大夫、集賢大學士，賞賚金帛，敕翰林丞旨歐陽玄製河平碑，以旌脫脫勞績，具載魯功，且宣付史館，并贈魯先臣三世。

translations.literal: The emperor was just then reading censorate ministers' memorials requesting commendation of Toghto's achievements in controlling the river; next they discussed Lu's merit; he was specially promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Academician-Expositor of the Hall for Advancing Worthies, rewarded with gold and silks, and ordered Academician-Recipient Ouyang Xuan of the Hanlin Academy to compose a stele on the pacified river to honor Toghto's labors, fully recording Lu's achievements, and also ordered it proclaimed and sent to the History Office, while enfeoffing Lu's ancestors for three generations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was just then reading memorials from censorate officials commending Toghto's achievements in controlling the river. Jia Lu's merits were discussed next. He was specially promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Academician-Expositor of the Hall for Advancing Worthies, rewarded with gold and silks, and ordered that Academician-Recipient Ouyang Xuan of the Hanlin Academy compose a stele commemorating the pacification of the river—honoring Toghto's labors while fully recording Jia Lu's achievements. The text was ordered proclaimed and deposited in the History Office, and honors were extended to three generations of Jia Lu's forebears.

sentences.zh: 尋拜中書左丞，從脫脫平徐州，脫脫既旋師，命魯追餘黨，分攻濠州，同緫兵官平章月可察兒督戰，魯誓師曰：「吾奉旨統八衛漢軍，頓兵于濠七日矣。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed left vice grand councillor of the Secretariat, followed Toghto in pacifying Xuzhou, and after Toghto withdrew his army was ordered to pursue remnant bands, dividing forces to attack Haozhou; together with the overall military commander and Pacification Commissioner Yexekä'r he supervised the campaign; Lu swore to the army, saying: "I have received orders to command the eight guards of Han troops and have stationed the army at Hao for seven days already.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed left vice grand councillor and accompanied Toghto in pacifying Xuzhou. After Toghto withdrew his army, Jia Lu was ordered to pursue remnant rebels and divide his forces to attack Haozhou. Pacification Commissioner Yexekä'r joined him as overall military commander. Jia Lu addressed the troops: "By imperial order I command the eight Han guard units. We have camped before Haozhou for seven days already.

sentences.zh: 爾諸將同心協力，必以今日巳、午時取城池，然後食。

translations.literal: You generals, with one heart and combined effort, must take the walled city by the si or wu hour today, and only then eat.
translations.idiomatic: You generals must act as one and take the city by the si or wu hour today—only then will you eat."

sentences.zh: 」魯上馬麾進，抵城下，忽頭眩下馬，且戒兵馬弗散，病愈亟，却藥不肯汗，竟卒于軍中，年五十七。

translations.literal: "Lu mounted his horse and waved the advance; reaching below the walls, he suddenly felt dizzy and dismounted, yet warned the troops not to disperse; his illness grew urgent, he refused medicine and would not sweat, and ultimately died in the army at age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted and led the charge to the foot of the walls, then suddenly grew dizzy and dismounted, ordering the troops not to scatter. His illness grew rapidly worse. He refused medicine that would induce sweating and died in camp at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月壬午也。

translations.literal: This was on the renwu day of the fifth month of the thirteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was on the renwu day of the fifth month of 1353.

sentences.zh: 月可察兒躬為治喪，選士護柩還高平，有旨賜交鈔五百錠以給葬事。

translations.literal: Yexekä'r personally arranged the funeral, selected gentlemen to escort the coffin back to Gaoping, and an edict granted five hundred ingots of paper money for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Yexekä'r personally arranged the funeral, selected officers to escort the coffin back to Gaoping, and an edict granted five hundred ingots of paper currency for funeral expenses.

sentences.zh: 子稹。

translations.literal: His son was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhen.

sentences.zh: 逯魯曾

translations.literal: Lu Luceng
translations.idiomatic: Lu Luceng

sentences.zh: 逯魯曾字善止，修武人。

translations.literal: Lu Luceng, style name Shanzhi, was a native of Xiuwu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Luceng, whose courtesy name was Shanzhi, came from Xiuwu.

sentences.zh: 性剛介，通經術，中天曆二年進士第，授翰林國史院編修官，辟御史臺掾，掌機密。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and upright; he mastered the Classics; in the second year of Tianshun he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed revising official of the Hanlin Academy National History Office, was recruited as secretarial aide of the Censorate, and handled confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and upright by nature, he mastered the classical canon. In 1329 he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed revising official at the Hanlin National History Office. Recruited as a secretarial aide at the Censorate, he handled confidential matters.

sentences.zh: 監察御史劾中丞史顯夫簡傲，魯曾開實封於大夫前曰：「中丞素持重，不能與人周旋，御史以人情劾之，非公論。

translations.literal: An investigating censor impeached Vice Censor-in-Chief Shi Xianfu for arrogance and aloofness; Luceng opened the sealed memorial before the great ministers and said: "The vice censor-in-chief has always been grave and weighty and cannot engage in social maneuvering; the censor impeaches him on personal grounds—this is not public judgment.
translations.idiomatic: When an investigating censor impeached Vice Censor-in-Chief Shi Xianfu for arrogance, Luceng opened the sealed memorial before the assembled ministers and said: "The vice censor-in-chief has always been grave and reserved and is no adept at social maneuvering. To impeach him on personal grounds is not impartial judgment.

sentences.zh: 」由是皆知其直。

translations.literal: "Thereby all knew his uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: From this everyone recognized his integrity.

sentences.zh: 除太常博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 武宗一廟，未立后主配享，集群臣廷議之。

translations.literal: For Emperor Wuzong's single temple, no principal consort had been established for joint sacrifice; the court gathered ministers for deliberation in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: For Emperor Wuzong's temple no principal consort had yet been designated for joint sacrifice, and the court convened the ministers for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 魯曾抗言：「先朝以武宗皇后真哥無子，不立其主。

translations.literal: Luceng spoke forthrightly: "The previous court, because Empress Zhenge of Emperor Wuzong had no son, did not establish her as principal consort.
translations.idiomatic: Luceng spoke forthrightly: "The previous court, because Empress Zhenge of Emperor Wuzong had borne no son, did not install her as principal consort.

sentences.zh: 」時伯顏為右丞相，以為明宗之母亦乞列氏，可以配享。

translations.literal: "At that time Bayan was right chancellor and held that the mother of Emperor Mingzong, of the Yilie clan, could serve for joint sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan was then right chancellor and held that the mother of Emperor Mingzong, of the Yilie clan, could serve for joint sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 徽政院傳太后旨，以文宗之母唐兀氏可以配享。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Palace Governance transmitted the empress dowager's decree that the mother of Emperor Wenzong, of the Tangut clan, could serve for joint sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Palace Governance transmitted the empress dowager's decree that the mother of Emperor Wenzong, of the Tangut clan, could serve for joint sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 伯顏問魯曾曰：「先朝既以真哥皇后無子，不為立主，今所立者，明宗母乎？

translations.literal: Bayan asked Luceng: "The previous court, since Empress Zhenge had no son, did not establish a principal consort—whom should we establish now, the mother of Mingzong?
translations.idiomatic: Bayan asked Luceng: "Since the previous court did not install a principal consort because Empress Zhenge had no son, whom should we install now—the mother of Mingzong?

sentences.zh: 文宗母乎？

translations.literal: Or the mother of Wenzong?
translations.idiomatic: Or the mother of Wenzong?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「真哥皇后在武宗朝，已膺玉冊，則為武宗皇后，明宗、文宗二母后，固為妾也。

translations.literal: "He replied: "Empress Zhenge in Emperor Wuzong's reign already received the jade register, and thus was Empress of Wuzong; the two empresses of Mingzong and Wenzong were by nature concubines.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Empress Zhenge had already received the jade register during Wuzong's reign and was therefore Wuzong's empress. The mothers of Mingzong and Wenzong were by status mere concubines.

sentences.zh: 今以無子之故，不為立主，以妾后為正宮，是為臣而廢先君之后，為子而追封先父之妾，於禮不可。

translations.literal: Now on the grounds of having no son, not establishing a principal consort but making a concubine empress the principal palace—this is as a subject abolishing the former ruler's empress, and as a son posthumously ennobling his father's concubine; by ritual it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: To refuse a principal consort because she bore no son, yet install a concubine empress in the principal place, is for a subject to displace his sovereign's empress and for a son to ennoble his father's concubine—this ritual cannot permit.

sentences.zh: 且燕王垂即位，追廢其母后，而立其生母為后，以配享先王，為萬世笑，豈可復蹈其失乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, when King Murong Chui of Yan took the throne, he posthumously deposed his empress and installed his birth mother as empress for joint sacrifice with the former king—a laughingstock for ten thousand generations; how can we repeat that error?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Murong Chui of Yan took the throne he deposed his empress and installed his birth mother in her place for joint sacrifice with the former king—a laughingstock for all posterity. How can we repeat that error?"

sentences.zh: 」集賢大學士陳顥，素嫉魯曾，出曰：「唐太宗冊曹王明之母為后，是亦二后也，豈不可乎？

translations.literal: "Academician-Expositor Chen Hao of the Hall for Advancing Worthies, who had long resented Luceng, came forward and said: "Tang Emperor Taizong ennobled the mother of Prince Cao as empress—were there not then two empresses? How can this not be permitted?
translations.idiomatic: Academician-Expositor Chen Hao of the Hall for Advancing Worthies, who had long resented Luceng, objected: "Emperor Taizong of Tang ennobled the mother of Prince Cao as empress—were there not then two empresses? Why should this not be permitted?"

sentences.zh: 」魯曾曰：「堯之母為帝嚳庶妃，堯立為帝，未聞冊以為后而配嚳。

translations.literal: "Luceng said: "Yao's mother was a secondary consort of Emperor Ku; when Yao was established as emperor, one never heard of her being enregistered as empress to share sacrifice with Ku.
translations.idiomatic: Luceng replied: "Yao's mother was a secondary consort of Emperor Ku. When Yao became emperor, no one ever heard of her being enregistered as empress to share sacrifice with Ku.

sentences.zh: 皇上為大元天子，不法堯、舜，而法唐太宗邪？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is Son of Heaven of the Great Yuan—will you not take Yao and Shun as law, but take Tang Emperor Taizong as law?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is Son of Heaven of the Great Yuan. Will you take Yao and Shun as your model, or Tang Emperor Taizong?"

sentences.zh: 」衆服其議，而伯顏韙之，遂以真哥皇后配焉。

translations.literal: "The assembly was convinced by his argument, and Bayan approved it; thereupon Empress Zhenge was established for joint sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly was convinced by his argument, Bayan approved it, and Empress Zhenge was duly installed for joint sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 復拜監察御史，劾荅失海牙、阿吉剌太尉，鞏卜班右丞，兀突蠻刑部尚書，吉當普監察御史，哈剌完者、月魯不花院使，呂思誠郎中，皆黜之。

translations.literal: He was again appointed investigating censor and impeached Grand Guardian Dashihaiya, Grand Guardian Ajila, Right Vice Councillor Gongbuban, Minister of Punishments Utuman, Investigating Censor Jidangpu, Court Commissioners Harqanju and Yelü Buhua, and Director Lü Sicheng—all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Reappointed investigating censor, he impeached Grand Guardian Dashihaiya, Grand Guardian Ajila, Right Vice Councillor Gongbuban, Minister of Punishments Utuman, Investigating Censor Jidangpu, Court Commissioners Harqanju and Yelü Buhua, and Director Lü Sicheng. All were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 八人之中，惟思誠少過，亦變祖宗選法，餘皆伯顏之黨，朝廷肅然。

translations.literal: Among the eight men, only Sicheng had minor faults, yet he too had altered the ancestral selection law; the rest were all Bayan's faction, and the court was solemnly awed.
translations.idiomatic: Of the eight, only Lü Sicheng was guilty of minor faults, and even he had altered the ancestral selection law. The rest were all Bayan's partisans. The court was sobered.

sentences.zh: 除樞密院都事，上言：「前伯顏專殺大臣，其黨利其妻女，巧誣以罪。

translations.literal: He was appointed director of affairs of the Bureau of Military Affairs and submitted a memorial: "Formerly Bayan arbitrarily executed great ministers; his faction coveted their wives and daughters and craftily framed them with crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed director of affairs at the Bureau of Military Affairs, he memorialized: "Formerly Bayan arbitrarily executed great ministers, and his faction coveted their wives and daughters and craftily framed them with crimes.

sentences.zh: 今大小官及諸人有罪，止坐其身，不得籍其妻女。

translations.literal: Now when officials great and small and all other persons are guilty, only they themselves should be punished; their wives and daughters must not be registered for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: When officials or private persons are now found guilty, only the offender himself should be punished. Their wives and daughters must not be registered for confiscation."

sentences.zh: 郯王為伯顏搆陷，妻女流離，當雪其無辜，給復子孫。

translations.literal: The Prince of Tan was framed by Bayan; his wife and daughters were displaced and scattered—they should be cleared of wrongful guilt and restoration granted to his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Tan was framed by Bayan, and his wife and daughters were driven into exile. Their innocence should be proclaimed and restoration granted to his descendants."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: "The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 除刑部員外郎，悉辨正橫罹伯顏所誣者。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Punishments and fully rectified those who had wrongly suffered Bayan's false accusations.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed vice director of the Ministry of Punishments, he fully rectified the cases of those wrongly accused by Bayan.

sentences.zh: 遷宗正府郎中，出為遼陽行省左右司郎中，除僉山北道肅政廉訪司事，入為禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of the Imperial Clan Court, sent out as director of the Left and Right Departments of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, appointed as commissioner of the Shanbei Surveillance Commission, and entered court as director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to director of the Imperial Clan Court, he was posted as director of the Left and Right Departments of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, appointed commissioner of the Shanbei Surveillance Commission, and recalled to serve as director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年，丞相脫脫討徐州賊，以官軍不習水土，募瀕海鹽丁為軍，乃超遷魯曾資善大夫、淮南宣慰使，領征討事，遣其募鹽丁五千人從征。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng, Chancellor Toghto campaigned against the Xuzhou bandits; because government troops were unaccustomed to the climate, he recruited coastal salt workers as soldiers; thereupon Luceng was specially promoted to Grand Master for the Good of the Heir Apparent and pacification commissioner of Huainan, placed in charge of the punitive campaign, and five thousand salt workers he recruited were sent to follow the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In 1352 Chancellor Toghto campaigned against the Xuzhou rebels. Because government troops were unaccustomed to the local climate, he recruited coastal salt workers as soldiers. Luceng was specially promoted to Grand Master for the Good of the Heir Apparent and pacification commissioner of Huainan, placed in charge of the punitive campaign, and five thousand salt workers he recruited were sent with the army.

sentences.zh: 徐州平，繼使領所部軍討淮東，卒於軍。

translations.literal: When Xuzhou was pacified, he was next ordered to lead his troops in campaigning east of the Huai and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuzhou was pacified he was ordered to lead his troops against the Huai east and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 貢師泰

translations.literal: Gong Shitai
translations.idiomatic: Gong Shitai

sentences.zh: 貢師泰字泰甫，寧國之宣城人。

translations.literal: Gong Shitai, style name Taifu, was a native of Xuancheng in Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Shitai, whose courtesy name was Taifu, came from Xuancheng in Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 父奎，以文學名家，延祐、至治間，官京師，為集賢直學士，卒，諡文靖。

translations.literal: His father Kui was famous for literary learning; between the Yanyou and Zhizhi reigns he served in the capital as direct academician of the Hall for Advancing Worthies; when he died he was given the posthumous title Cultivated and Tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kui was renowned for literary learning. During the Yanyou and Zhizhi reigns he served in the capital as direct academician of the Hall for Advancing Worthies. At his death he received the posthumous title Cultivated and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 師泰早肄業國子學為諸生。

translations.literal: Shitai early pursued his studies at the Imperial University as a student.
translations.idiomatic: Shitai studied early at the Imperial University as a student.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年，釋褐出身，授從仕郎、太和州判官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiding, he left student robes and entered office, appointed Gentleman for Attendance and assistant prefect of Taihe prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1327 he left student robes for official service and was appointed Gentleman for Attendance and assistant prefect of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，改徽州路歙縣丞，江浙行省辟為掾，尋以土著，自劾去。

translations.literal: He mourned his father, was changed to assistant magistrate of She county on the Huizhou circuit, was recruited as secretariat aide by the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat, but soon because he was a native of the place impeached himself and left.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was appointed assistant magistrate of She county on the Huizhou circuit. The Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat recruited him as a secretariat aide, but he soon resigned on the ground that, as a native of the district, he ought not hold the post.

sentences.zh: 大臣有以其名聞者，擢應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: A great minister who had heard his name recommended him, and he was promoted to Hanlin literary attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When a senior minister heard his name he was recommended and promoted to Hanlin literary attendant.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，服闋，除紹興路緫管府推官，郡有疑獄，悉為詳讞而剖決之。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; when mourning ended he was appointed judicial investigator of the Shaoxing circuit general administration, and in doubtful cases of the prefecture he fully reviewed the verdicts and decided them.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was appointed judicial investigator for the Shaoxing circuit administration. In every doubtful case in the prefecture he reviewed the records in detail and rendered judgment.

sentences.zh: 山陰白洋港有大船飄近岸，史甲二十人，適取鹵海濱，見其無主，因取其篙櫓，而船中有二死人。

translations.literal: At Baiyang Harbor in Shanyin a large ship drifted near shore; twenty men surnamed Shi, who happened to be gathering brine by the sea, saw it had no owner and took its poles and oars, while in the ship were two dead men.
translations.idiomatic: At Baiyang Harbor in Shanyin a large ship drifted ashore. Twenty men surnamed Shi, who happened to be gathering brine along the coast, saw that it had no owner and took its poles and oars. Inside the ship were two dead men.

sentences.zh: 有徐乙者，怪其無物而有死人，稱為史等所劫。

translations.literal: A man named Xu Yi found it strange that there were no goods but there were dead men, and claimed that Shi and the others had robbed them.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Xu Yi found it strange that the ship held no cargo yet contained corpses, and accused Shi and the others of robbery and murder.

sentences.zh: 史傭作富民高丙家，事遂連高。

translations.literal: Shi was hired labor in the household of the wealthy man Gao Bing, and the affair thus implicated Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was a hired laborer in the household of the wealthy man Gao Bing, and the case thus implicated Gao as well.

sentences.zh: 史既誣服，高亦就逮。

translations.literal: Shi, having been forced by false confession, Gao was also arrested.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi was forced into a false confession, Gao was arrested as well.

sentences.zh: 師泰密詢之，則里中沈丁載物抵杭而回，漁者張網海中，因盜網中魚，為漁者所殺，史實未嘗殺人奪物，高亦弗知情，其冤皆白。

translations.literal: Shitai secretly inquired and learned that Shen Ding of the village, carrying goods to Hangzhou and returning, had cast nets in the sea; because he stole fish from the nets he was killed by the fishermen; Shi in truth had never killed men or seized goods, and Gao also did not know— their wrongful guilt was all cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Shitai made secret inquiries and learned that a villager named Shen Ding, returning from carrying goods to Hangzhou, had cast nets in the sea and was killed by fishermen when he stole fish from their nets. Shi had never killed anyone or seized goods, and Gao knew nothing of the affair. The innocence of both men was established.

sentences.zh: 游徼徐裕，以巡鹽為名，肆暴村落間。

translations.literal: Patrol officer Xu Yu, under the name of inspecting salt, committed violence wantonly among the villages.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol officer Xu Yu, under the pretext of inspecting salt, committed violence wantonly in the villages.

sentences.zh: 一日，遇諸暨商，奪其所齎錢，撲殺之，投尸於水，走告縣曰：「我獲私鹽犯人，畏罪赴水死矣。

translations.literal: One day he met a merchant from Zhuji, seized the money he carried, beat him to death, threw the corpse in the water, and ran to report to the county: "I captured a private-salt offender; fearing guilt he went into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: One day he met a merchant from Zhuji, seized his money, beat him to death, and threw the body into the water. He then ran to the county office and reported: "I captured a private-salt offender who, fearing punishment, threw himself into the water and drowned."

sentences.zh: 」官驗視，以有傷，疑之。

translations.literal: "The officials examined the body and, finding wounds, were suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Officials examined the body, found wounds, and grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 遂以疑獄釋。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was released as a doubtful case.
translations.idiomatic: The case was released as doubtful.

sentences.zh: 師泰追詢覆按之，具得裕所以殺人狀，復俾待報。

translations.literal: Shitai pursued inquiry and re-examined it, fully obtaining the circumstances of Yu's killing, and again had him held awaiting report.
translations.idiomatic: Shitai pursued the inquiry and re-examined the case, fully establishing how Xu Yu had committed the murder, and had him held pending final judgment.

sentences.zh: 餘姚孫國賓，以求盜，獲姚甲造偽鈔，受賕而釋之，執高乙、魯丙赴有司，誣以同造偽。

translations.literal: Sun Guobin of Yuyao, in pursuit of thieves, captured Yao Jia making counterfeit notes, accepted a bribe and released him, seized Gao Yi and Lu Bing and sent them to the authorities, falsely accusing them of jointly making counterfeits.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Guobin of Yuyao, while pursuing thieves, captured Yao Jia making counterfeit notes, accepted a bribe and released him, then seized Gao Yi and Lu Bing and sent them to the authorities on a false charge of joint counterfeiting.

sentences.zh: 高嘗為姚行用，實非自造，孫既舍姚，因加罪於高，而魯與孫有隙，故并連之，魯與高未嘗相識也。

translations.literal: Gao had once been employed by Yao and in truth had not made counterfeits himself; Sun, having already released Yao, therefore added guilt to Gao, while Lu had a grudge with Sun and was thus implicated together—Lu and Gao had never known each other.
translations.idiomatic: Gao had once worked for Yao and had not himself counterfeited. Sun, having released Yao, shifted the guilt onto Gao. Lu bore a grudge against Sun and was implicated as well—though Lu and Gao had never even met.

sentences.zh: 師泰疑高等覆造不合，以孫詰之，辭屈而情見。

translations.literal: Shitai doubted that Gao and the others' repeated counterfeiting did not fit, questioned Sun, and his words were defeated while the truth appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Shitai found the charge of repeated counterfeiting against Gao implausible and questioned Sun, whose testimony collapsed and exposed the truth.

sentences.zh: 即釋魯而加高以本罪，姚遂處死，孫亦就法。

translations.literal: He immediately released Lu and imposed on Gao the original crime; Yao was then executed, and Sun also received the law.
translations.idiomatic: He released Lu and imposed on Gao only the crime he had actually committed. Yao was executed, and Sun was punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 其於冤獄詳讞之明多類此。

translations.literal: His clarity in detailed review of wrongful cases was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His clarity in reviewing wrongful convictions was mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 以故郡民自以不冤，治行為諸郡第一。

translations.literal: For this reason the people of the prefecture considered themselves not wronged, and his administrative conduct ranked first among all prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the people of the prefecture believed themselves free of injustice, and his administrative record ranked first among all prefectures.

sentences.zh: 考滿，復入翰林為應奉，預修后妃、功臣列傳，事畢，遷宣文閣授經郎，歷翰林待制、國子司業，擢禮部郎中，再遷吏部，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: When his term evaluation was complete, he again entered the Hanlin as literary attendant, participated in compiling the biographies of empresses and meritorious ministers; when the work was finished he was transferred to lecturer of the Xuanwen Pavilion, served as Hanlin attendant, vice chancellor of the Imperial University, was promoted to director of the Ministry of Rites, was again transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When his term was complete he returned to the Hanlin as literary attendant and helped compile the biographies of empresses and meritorious ministers. When the work was finished he was transferred to lecturer of the Xuanwen Pavilion, served as Hanlin attendant and vice chancellor of the Imperial University, was promoted to director of the Ministry of Rites, transferred again to the Ministry of Personnel, and appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 自世祖以後，省臺之職，南人斥不用，及是，始復舊制，於是南士復得居省臺，自師泰始，時論以為得人。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Shizu, southerners had been rejected from Secretariat and Censorate posts; at this time the old system was restored, and thus southern scholars again could hold Secretariat and Censorate posts—beginning with Shitai; contemporary opinion held that worthy men had been obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Shizu's reign southerners had been barred from Secretariat and Censorate posts. Now the old system was restored, and southern scholars could again hold such offices—beginning with Shitai. Contemporary opinion held that the court had at last found the right men.

sentences.zh: 至正十四年，除吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng, he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1354 he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時江淮兵起，京師食不足，師泰奉命和糴于浙右，得糧百萬石，以給京師。

translations.literal: At that time warfare arose on the Jiang-Huai, and the capital's food was insufficient; Shitai received orders to purchase grain in western Zhe and obtained one million piculs of grain to supply the capital.
translations.idiomatic: War had broken out along the Jiang-Huai, and the capital faced food shortages. Shitai was ordered to purchase grain in western Zhe and obtained one million piculs to supply the capital.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以京師至上都，驛戶凋弊，命師泰巡視整飭之。

translations.literal: The court, because relay households between the capital and the Upper Capital were depleted and distressed, ordered Shitai to inspect and rectify them.
translations.idiomatic: Because relay households along the route from the capital to the Upper Capital were depleted and distressed, the court ordered Shitai to inspect and reorganize them.

sentences.zh: 至則歷究其病原，驗其富貧，而均其徭役，數十郡之民，賴以稍蘇。

translations.literal: When he arrived he thoroughly traced the roots of the disease, verified rich and poor, and equalized their corvée labor; the people of several tens of prefectures relied on this to recover somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he traced the roots of the abuse, assessed rich and poor households, and equalized their corvée burdens. The people of dozens of prefectures were thereby given some relief.

sentences.zh: 豪貴以其不利於己，深嫉之，然莫能有所中傷也。

translations.literal: Powerful families, because this was not to their advantage, deeply resented him, yet could not find means to injure him.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families deeply resented him because his reforms harmed their interests, yet they could find no means to injure him.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷欲仍和糴浙西，因除師泰都水庸田使。

translations.literal: When the court wished again to purchase grain in western Zhe, Shitai was accordingly appointed Commissioner of Water Control and Wasteland Reclamation.
translations.idiomatic: When the court wished again to purchase grain in western Zhe, Shitai was appointed Commissioner of Water Control and Wasteland Reclamation.

sentences.zh: 十五年，庸田司罷，擢江西廉訪副使，未行，遷福建廉訪使，居亡何，除禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the Wasteland Office was abolished; he was promoted to vice surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi, but before departing was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Fujian; after a short while he was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1355 the Wasteland Office was abolished. He was promoted to vice surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi but, before departing, was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Fujian. Shortly afterward he was appointed minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 時平江缺守，廷議難其人，師泰又以選為平江路緫管。

translations.literal: At that time Pingjiang lacked a prefect; court deliberation found no suitable man, and Shitai was again selected as general administrator of Pingjiang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Pingjiang then lacked a prefect, and the court could find no suitable candidate. Shitai was again selected as general administrator of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，甫視事，張士誠自高郵率衆渡江，直抵城下，攻圍甚急。

translations.literal: That winter, just as he assumed office, Zhang Shicheng from Gaoyou led his host across the river, came straight to below the walls, and pressed the siege fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, just as he assumed office, Zhang Shicheng led his forces from Gaoyou across the Yangzi, came straight to the city walls, and laid siege with great urgency.

sentences.zh: 明年春，守將弗能支，斬關遁去，師泰領義兵出戰，力不敵，亦懷印綬棄城遁，匿海濱者久之。

translations.literal: The next spring the defending generals could not hold; they cut through the pass and fled; Shitai led militia out to fight, his strength was not equal, and he too took his seal and sash and abandoned the city to flee, hiding by the seashore for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring the defenders could not hold. They cut through the gate and fled. Shitai led militia out to fight but was overpowered. He too took his seal and sash, abandoned the city, and hid along the coast for a long time.

sentences.zh: 士誠既納降，江浙行省丞相達識帖睦邇，以便宜授師泰兩浙都轉運鹽使。

translations.literal: After Shicheng had submitted, Dashi Timur, chancellor of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat, by discretionary authority appointed Shitai Commissioner of Salt Transport for the Two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Shicheng submitted, Dashi Timur, chancellor of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat, appointed Shitai by discretionary authority Commissioner of Salt Transport for the Two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 至則剔其積蠹，通其利源，大課以集，國用資之。

translations.literal: When he arrived he eliminated accumulated abuses, opened profit sources, and great revenue was gathered; state expenditure relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he eliminated accumulated abuses, opened new sources of revenue, and gathered substantial tax receipts on which state expenditure came to rely.

sentences.zh: 丞相復承制除師泰江浙行省參知政事。

translations.literal: The chancellor again, by imperial commission, appointed Shitai participant in government of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor again appointed him, by imperial commission, participant in government of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十年，朝廷除戶部尚書，俾分部閩中，以閩鹽易糧，由海道轉運給京師，凡為糧數十萬石，朝廷賴焉。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the court appointed him Minister of Revenue, ordering him to divide duties in Fujian, exchanging Fujian salt for grain and transporting it by sea route to supply the capital—altogether several hundred thousand piculs of grain on which the court relied.
translations.idiomatic: In 1360 the court appointed him minister of revenue and ordered him to oversee Fujian, exchanging Fujian salt for grain and shipping it by sea to supply the capital—several hundred thousand piculs in all on which the court came to rely.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，召為祕書卿，行至杭之海寧，得疾而卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was summoned as Secretary Director; en route he reached Haining in Hangzhou, took ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1362 he was summoned as Secretary Director. En route he reached Haining in Hangzhou, fell ill, and died.

sentences.zh: 師泰性倜儻，狀貌偉然，既以文字知名，而於政事尤長，所至績效輒暴著。

translations.literal: Shitai's nature was free and unrestrained, his appearance grand; though famous for writing, he was especially skilled in government affairs, and wherever he went his achievements were suddenly conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: Shitai was free-spirited and imposing in appearance. Though famous as a writer, he was especially skilled in administration, and wherever he served his achievements were immediately conspicuous.

sentences.zh: 尤喜接引後進，士之賢，不問識不識，即加推轂，以故士譽翕然咸歸之。

translations.literal: He especially delighted in guiding and advancing the younger generation; for worthy scholars, whether he knew them or not, he immediately promoted them; for this reason scholarly reputation converged and all turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: He especially delighted in guiding younger scholars. For any worthy man, whether he knew him or not, he would at once lend his support. For this reason scholarly reputation converged upon him.

sentences.zh: 有詩文若干卷行于世。

translations.literal: He had poetry and prose in several juan circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected poetry and prose, comprising several juan, circulated in his lifetime.

sentences.zh: 周伯琦

translations.literal: Zhou Boqi
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Boqi

sentences.zh: 周伯琦字伯溫，饒州人。

translations.literal: Zhou Boqi, style name Bowen, was a native of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Boqi, whose courtesy name was Bowen, came from Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 父應極，至大間，仁宗為皇太子，召見，獻皇元頌，為言于武宗，以為翰林待制。

translations.literal: His father Yingji, during the Zhida period when Renzong was crown prince, was summoned for audience, presented an Ode to the Primal Origin of the Sovereign, spoke of it to Wuzong, and was made Hanlin attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingji, during the Zhida period when Renzong was crown prince, was summoned to audience and presented an Ode to the Primal Origin of the Sovereign. He spoke of it to Wuzong and was appointed Hanlin attendant.

sentences.zh: 後為皇太子說書，日侍英邸。

translations.literal: Later he was lecturer to the crown prince and daily attended the princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as lecturer to the crown prince and attended daily at the princely residence.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，遷集賢待制，終池州路同知緫管府事。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, he was transferred to attendant of the Hall for Advancing Worthies and ended as associate general administrator of Chizhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne he was transferred to attendant of the Hall for Advancing Worthies and ended his career as associate general administrator of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 伯琦自幼從宦，游京師，入國學，為上舍生，積分及高等。

translations.literal: Boqi from youth followed his father's official career, traveled to the capital, entered the Imperial University as a senior dormitory student, and accumulated credits to the highest grade.
